prompt: Analyze whether API latency materially changed during an incident window using request metrics, deployment events, traffic mix, and partial telemetry. One region lost 20% of samples and traffic shifted toward an expensive endpoint at the same time. Reconstruct the timeline, normalize/segment enough to separate mix shift from within-endpoint latency, quantify missingness and uncertainty, and report what evidence supports versus does not support. Do not perform the debugging fix itself.

requirements: time-bucketed latency/traffic by endpoint and region around a defined incident window
deployment markers plus known 20% telemetry loss in one region
pre/post traffic-mix change toward a high-latency endpoint
reproducible calculations for weighted aggregate and within-segment comparisons
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot

evidence: Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification
hierarchy boundary and specialist selection rationale
source/version boundary when facts can drift

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The result must establish the actual operational-data-analysis boundary and relevant environment before acting, preserve the hierarchy relationship (broader=data-analysis; children=finops-cloud-cost; near-neighbor=analytics-engineering), and not absorb the near-neighbor responsibility merely because it is adjacent.
Operational conclusions distinguish aggregate mix effects, within-segment changes, and telemetry gaps; missing data cannot be silently treated as healthy traffic.
Metric lineage; Baseline rationale; Decision-linked findings
The result must not treat a happy path, generated artifact, compilation, or unsupported assumption as sufficient proof of operational-data-analysis correctness.

Every material completion claim must map to observable evidence (Metric lineage; Baseline rationale; Decision-linked findings; Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale), with simulated, unavailable, inferred, stale, or unresolved evidence labeled rather than converted into certainty.
